title: Pinatubo chili (Pinatubo F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Pinatubo chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Pinatubo chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety, also sold or known as Pinatubo F1 or Condor Pinatubo F1. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Pinatubo chili is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Pinatubo F1 or Condor Pinatubo F1, this is the same chili. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [chili variety finder](/crop-varieties/chili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 75 to 80 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Hot chili sold for the siling labuyo market but longer than native labuyo: 6 to 8 cm, about 4 g, very hot (seller gives 80,000 to 200,000 Scoville units), about 200 fruits to the kilo.
Handles stress, notably in the rainy season (seller).
For fresh sale or for sauces and chili powder.
Plants can bear for six months to a year with good care (Allied, in Agriculture Monthly).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: agriculture Monthly stories: a Sto. Tomas, Batangas grower harvested about a ton a month from 2,500 sq m, and Allied says food processors buy it for hot sauce, also in Harbest's catalogue. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual chili on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Pinatubo chili

Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Pinatubo F1 the same as Pinatubo?
items.a: Yes. Pinatubo F1 is another name for Pinatubo. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pinatubo?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
